topics.topic: Section eligibility rules for creating or updating SectionProgress
questions: Can staff set progress for a project section that has no plan in the active budget version, has zero planned work, or belongs only to an inactive version?
Which PortalSections may a staff progress update create or change a SectionProgress record for?
Must a section currently have positive planned work in the active budget version before staff may create or update its SectionProgress?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about progress-update eligibility already decided by P16.

precedent.topic: Whether SectionProgress is allowed without planned work in the active budget version
quotes:
the section is this project's (`budget_management.validate_project_section`,
before the transaction)
precedent.why: The later operation validates project ownership only, so an absent or zero-work section remains a valid update target if it belongs to the project.

topics.topic: Effect of client_visible=false on viewer photo reads
questions: Does a viewer-facing photo read exclude ProgressPhoto records with `client_visible = false`, or return their PhotoView metadata while refusing only the binary?
For a ClientViewer, does `client_visible = false` hide the entire ProgressPhoto from gallery reads, or only prohibit its binary download?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about filtering non-client-visible photos from viewer gallery results already decided by P14.

precedent.topic: Viewer gallery treatment of photos with client_visible false
quotes:
`ProgressPhotoView` list by `photo_date` then `photo_id`, ascending; for a
viewer only client-visible photos; never `file_ref` or `intake_id`; empty
when none.
precedent.why: The later photo-list operation filters non-client-visible photos out of viewer results.

topics.topic: Handling replayed photo intake IDs with changed content
questions: How must publication handle an existing `intake_id` whose newly supplied content differs from the stored ProgressPhoto?
What happens when a PhotoPublication repeats an existing `intake_id` with content different from the stored ProgressPhoto?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about replaying a photo intake_id with different content already decided by P18.

precedent.topic: The outcome of replaying an intake_id with conflicting photo content
quotes:
`PhotoValidationError` for a publication of another project or a section
outside it; `PhotoConflictError` for a replay that differs or belongs to
another project.
precedent.why: The public operation rejects reuse of intake_id with differing content or another project.

questions: What is the entity identity of SectionProgress: the existing `section_id`, the `(project_id, section_id)` pair, or a separate portal-minted progress identifier omitted from the field list?
What is the identity of a SectionProgress entity, and what identifier names it in repositories, references, and audit records?

quotes:
None: the tables `config.persistence.section_progress_table_name` (key
`project_id`, `section_id`) and `config.persistence.work_payment_table_name`
(key `payment_id`) exist, one column per field of `SectionProgress` and
`WorkPayment`.
judgement.why: The later repository contract makes the SectionProgress record key the composite of project_id and section_id; representation of that key in repository or audit formats is later-state encoding detail.

topics.topic: Whether credentials may be issued or re-issued for a revoked viewer
questions: Can an administrator issue or re-issue a credential for a terminally revoked ClientViewer?
May an administrator issue or re-issue a ViewerAccessCredential for a revoked ClientViewer?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about issuing a ViewerAccessCredential for a revoked viewer already decided by P3.

quotes:
### Errors

Access-management failures; `ScopedNotFoundError` for an unknown or
non-active viewer.
precedent.why: The later public operation refuses issuance for a revoked, hence non-active, viewer.

topics.topic: Whether first-administrator bootstrap creates an audit record
questions: Does successful creation of the first administrator append an AuditRecord?
Does successful first-administrator bootstrap create an AuditRecord?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged bootstrap-audit question already decided by P10; R0-07's prohibition concerns exposing or auditing the supplied email and password, not the staff.create action.

precedent.topic: Whether first-administrator bootstrap creates an AuditRecord
quotes:
The first-administrator bootstrap of R0-07 is no exception: it writes one
  `staff.create` record with actor kind `system`, no actor, no project and
  the new `staff_id` as entity; the email and password it was given appear
  in no record.
precedent.why: State 1 explicitly requires the bootstrap audit and clarifies that R0-07's non-auditing rule applies to the supplied email and password.

topics.topic: Whether producer grants may be created for an all-projects principal
questions: Can a ProducerProjectGrant be created for a ServicePrincipal whose immutable `scope_mode` is `all_projects`?
Can an administrator create a ProducerProjectGrant for a ServicePrincipal whose scope_mode is `all_projects`?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about creating a ProducerProjectGrant for an all-projects principal already decided by P5.

precedent.topic: ProducerProjectGrant eligibility for disabled or all-projects principals
quotes:
### Errors

Access-management failures; `ScopedNotFoundError` for a project the Registry
does not know or an unknown principal; `ArchivedProjectRejected` for an
inactive project; `AuthorizationRejected` for an existing active grant;
`RegistryBoundaryError`.
precedent.why: The later operation's closed failures impose no active-principal or granted_projects-scope precondition, so grants may be created for disabled and all-projects principals.

topics.topic: Whether project grants may be created for a revoked viewer
questions: May an administrator create the sole `(viewer_id, project_id)` grant record when the viewer is already revoked?
May a new ProjectViewerGrant be created for a revoked ClientViewer?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about creating a ProjectViewerGrant for a revoked viewer already decided by P7.

precedent.topic: ProjectViewerGrant creation for a revoked ClientViewer
quotes:
### Errors

Access-management failures; `RegistryBoundaryError` carrying the validation's
failure kind for a project the Registry does not know or does not report
active, and for a failed Registry call; `ScopedNotFoundError` for an unknown
or non-active viewer; `AuthorizationRejected` for an existing active grant.
precedent.why: The later grant operation refuses a revoked viewer as non-active.

topics.topic: Action that updates ExpenseAllocation provenance fields
questions: What product action, if any, sets `updated_at` and `updated_by` on an ExpenseAllocation?

topics.topic: Activation behavior when an imported version omits an allocated section
questions: When a candidate imported version omits a section targeted by an existing allocation, does activation succeed and expose an unresolved allocation, or is activation refused until re-allocation?

quotes:
Sections of the previous
version absent from the new one keep their identity and history; their
allocations become *unresolved against the active version* (a derived state,
not a stored flag) and must be explicitly re-allocated by an operator.

activation of a version is refused while any section
allocation would be unresolved against it, and no other mapping operation
exists.
judgement.divergence: One passage permits activation and leaves the existing allocation unresolved against the newly active version; the other refuses activation until the allocation is changed, which the activating operator and later readers observe.
judgement.why: The two State 1 passages give opposite lifecycle outcomes for the same activation attempt when an existing allocation targets a section omitted by the candidate version.

witness.initial: Project P has active budget version V1, and an existing expense allocation targets section A; candidate imported version V2 has no plan for A.
events: An authorized operator attempts to activate V2 without first reallocating the expense.
outcomes: V2 becomes active and the allocation becomes unresolved against the active version.
Activation is refused and V1 remains active.
witness.observer: The operator sees success versus refusal, and authorized readers see V2 versus the unchanged V1.
basis:
existing allocations require explicit mapping to the sections of the newly
  activated version; matching stable section identifiers may link
  automatically; a renamed section with the same stable identifier remains
  the same section; sections without a stable correspondence require manual
  mapping; matching by display name alone is forbidden;

For an active project an operator can: correct, include, or exclude an
expense; allocate or manually split it across sections or `Other expenses`
(allocation sum equals the expense total; automatic proportional split is
forbidden); update manual work progress per section (0–100%); register work
payments (idempotent by stable payment identity); publish progress photos and
manage caption, section association, and visibility; maintain the manual
budget; review and activate imported budget versions.

topics.topic: Allowed transitions into disabled StaffAccount status
questions: May an administrator disable an active or pending-verification account directly, or may `disabled` be entered only from `suspended`?

quotes:
StaffStatus:      pending_verification → active;  active ↔ suspended;
                  active|suspended → disabled (terminal)
judgement.why: The later status-transition table permits disabling an active or suspended account, but not disabling a pending-verification account directly.

topics.topic: Creation and initial status of the first manual BudgetVersion
questions: When the first manual-section upsert is made for a project with no manual BudgetVersion, does that action mint the manual BudgetVersion, and if so is it initially active or inactive?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about creation and initial status of the first manual BudgetVersion already decided by P19.

precedent.topic: When and by whom a project's manual BudgetVersion is created
quotes: `module:budget_management`. Return the project's one manual budget version, creating it empty when absent.

A18: at most one manual version per project; a new one is `inactive` and is
never activated implicitly; A13 (`budget.manual_version_create` only when it
is created).

A18 (stable
`PortalSection` identity; imported plans never change; a missing manual
version is created as `ensure_manual_budget` does)
precedent.why: The later API defines ensure_manual_budget and also makes the first manual-section upsert create a missing manual version.

topics.topic: Scope of payment_id uniqueness and idempotency
questions: If the same `payment_id` is submitted for two different projects, is the second request a conflict, a distinct payment under project-scoped uniqueness, or a replay of the first payment?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about reuse of payment_id across projects already decided by P24.

precedent.topic: The outcome of replaying payment_id with conflicting payment facts
quotes:
`TrackingConflictError` for a
replay of the id with other content or of another project, changing nothing.
precedent.why: The later operation rejects a payment_id replay carrying different payment facts.
